messages:
sam.partnerships: FYI OpenWeightsCo pushed ModelX-v2 artifacts into their shared bucket. I downloaded the manifest and LICENSE.md. We need to decide what lane we can offer partners: marketplace listing, hosted API, Dedicated, or SI installs. Opening the thread for legal + engineering intake.
tara-legal: I reviewed LICENSE.md. It's labelled 'for research use only' and disallows commercial exploitation. That blocks marketplace and Dedicated resales. It also lacks a clear export control statement; we need supplier confirmation on jurisdiction and any sanctioned-country restrictions.
nate-eng: Tech check: the bundle contains raw FP32 checkpoints, tokenizer vocab, and a conversion script that shells out to a closed-source converter binary. The runtime also expects a custom fused-attn kernel that isn't present. If they won't allow redistributing raw weights, we can still support a hosted endpoint but need a hosting license + provenance.
anya-ops: Ops red flag: the S3 ACLs grant their CI role broad access. Do not accept direct cross-account roles. Ask them to provide presigned, time-limited URLs and a signed artifact list (SHA256). Also prefer object locking off until we verify checksums.
ben-partners: Spoke briefly with OWCo PM: they're protective of raw weights and want to avoid GPL-style leakage. They're open to a Marketplace listing if we agree to no-checkpoint redistribution and clear attribution. I'll propose two tracks to them.
claudia-ml: From model-ops POV: we need either kernel source or a vetted, versioned binary with checksum and license to ship with our runtime. Additionally, request a small curated eval set (50 prompts) and baseline outputs to validate parity after any quantization. Without that we can't certify performance.
sam.partnerships: Tara  what minimal clauses let us list on Marketplace (hosted + metadata listing) while protecting their IP? Can we do 'no raw checkpoint distribution' plus hosting permissions?
tara-legal: Yes. Draft minimal terms: a Distribution License Addendum (DLA) granting Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide right to host and serve the model and to distribute compiled/quantized runtime artifacts to Redwood customers, while expressly prohibiting redistribution of raw checkpoints. Supplier retains copyright and moral rights. Require signed manifest (SHA256) and a provenance file as precondition. Also include cooperation on export compliance.
nate-eng: Operational asks to include with DLA: 1) signed manifest with SHA256 per-file, 2) provenance + build steps for reproducibility, 3) compatibility doc (max context, tokenization norms, FP16/INT8 support), 4) a small smoke test script and eval set.
anya-ops: For SI/on-prem lane: if supplier refuses raw transfers, we can provide a sealed 'installer image' under a restricted redistributable that SIs can pull under NDA. Need supplier consent to distribute the image to SI accounts and an audit log requirement.
ate-ben: (typo in chat) ben-partners: I'll send two lanes in the outreach: 1) Marketplace/Hosted listing (requires DLA + manifest + provenance + hosting license) and 2) SI/Dedicated (requires DLA + SOW + KYC + explicit SI transfer permission).
sam.partnerships: Tara please paste a short starter clause we can include in the email to speed negotiation.
tara-legal: Starter clause: 
```
Grant: Supplier grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, sublicensable license to host, serve, and distribute compiled/quantized runtime artifacts and containers to Redwood customers. Redistribution of raw checkpoints and raw uncompiled weights is prohibited. Commercial use by Redwood customers is permitted. Supplier retains all IP rights and may require attribution.
Provenance & Integrity: Each release must include a signed manifest (SHA256) and a provenance file detailing build steps, converter versions, and kernel dependencies.
Export & Compliance: Supplier represents any export or sanctions restrictions and will cooperate on required licenses. SI/on-prem transfers require additional KYC and an executed SOW.
```
Add clause that we will not ship their closed-source converter binary to SIs unless they provide a redistributable binary + checksum.
claudia-ml: Also include a kernel/ops disclosure: indicate whether fused kernels are closed-source and whether a redistributable binary with a stable ABI will be provided. We need to know memory/per-token numbers for our model card.
nate-eng: And a runtime compatibility matrix: supported context lengths, beam/greedy behavior, tokenizer normalization, and expected throughput for small/medium/large batch profiles. We'll include those metrics in the console model profile.
sam.partnerships: Ben  ask them to fill the checklist in one email: license acceptance (yes/no), provide manifest, kernel binary/source option, eval set, export declarations, acceptance of DLA draft. We need to lock terms in 2 weeks to hit marketing01s joint announcement window.
ben-partners: Drafting now and will loop OWCo legal + eng. I'll paste their reply here. :rocket:
deploy-bot: created JIRA PARTNERS-421: "OpenWeightsCo DLA & packaging"  assignee: ben-partners.
